solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protest — Conservative rotter is a US politician

parts.note: a demo is a short word for a protest march
a rat is a contemptible person, a rotter

explanation.surface: A disgruntled Tory brands someone a rotter at a protest, and the rotter turns out to be an American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of one of the two main American parties are called by this name.

clue.text: Song about an aromatic plant

indicators.note: about means the song goes around the other piece

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A song written about a sweet-smelling plant.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a herb of the mint family, noted for its fragrant leaves, grown in Crete.

clue.text: Parent, one kept over time?

definitions.meaning: a familiar word for a mother
an embalmed body preserved for centuries, as in ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A parent who has been looked after for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mother and an embalmed, preserved corpse.

clue.text: Communication for all observed: a tool

parts.note: a circular is a letter sent to many people
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A memo sent to all staff has been seen and turns out to be about a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A power tool with a rotating toothed disc used for cutting wood.

clue.text: Cunning manipulation of statue

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and reshaping, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sly piece of handiwork moving a sculpture around.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and clever, quick to spot an advantage.

clue.text: Go crazy, flipping

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it is read from the end backwards

parts.note: bats is informal for crazy, as in having bats in the belfry

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go wild, losing their temper completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like an angry intensifier but turns BATS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a go, an attempt.

clue.text: Three stumble over hindrance

indicators.note: over places the first word above the second in a down entry

parts.note: trip means stumble
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Three people trip over an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three, such as three notes played in the time of two, or three babies born together.

clue.text: Money that may have risen?

explanation.surface: Cash that might have gone up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for cash, and a loaf is made from dough that rises.

clue.text: Watch, perhaps, to send back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for sending in the opposite direction

parts.note: to remit is to send, especially money

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about returning a wristwatch to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch can be used as a device for measuring time, so it is an example of one; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Leading team getting a cut

parts.note: top means leading, as in the top team
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: The team at the top of the league is taking a share of the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cut' reads as a share of profits; it is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef taken from the hindquarter, a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Tape nearly stretched over a box in sport

indicators.note: stretched suggests the letters are pulled out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tape nearly pulled across a box, as when marking out a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the penalty area is known as 'the box'.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked rectangle in front of a football goal is commonly called the box.

clue.text: A US city, it doesn't matter which?

parts.note: NY is New York, the American city

explanation.surface: Someone asked to pick an American city shrugs that any will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'whichever one, I'm not fussy' is the sense of this determiner.

clue.text: Going straight again, and let out with gun!

indicators.note: out signals the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal has been released from prison and, alarmingly, has been handed a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going straight' suggests a reformed criminal; here it means made straight again, as knotted string is.
explanation.definitionFit: Knots and tangles removed, a rope or hair is straightened out once more.

clue.text: Country is behind you, the farmer

indicators.note: is behind places the country after the old word for you

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A farmer is told that his whole country is supporting him.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was a small landowner who farmed his own land.

clue.text: Nothing to restrain view

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to pinion is to restrain by holding the arms

explanation.surface: There is nothing to block the sight of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' looks like a sight; it means a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or judgement someone holds.

clue.text: Fantastic result for Irish province

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wonderful outcome for one of Ireland's provinces, perhaps in sport or an election.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the northern of Ireland's four historic provinces, often used for Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Under first of Rembrandts, I place false copy

indicators.note: under places the rearranged letters below the initial in a down entry
first of means take the opening letter of the painter's name
false means the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A forger hangs a fake beneath a genuine Rembrandt.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact reproduction of an original, such as a painting.

clue.text: Soft bed for an actor

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a bed is a layer, as of rock

explanation.surface: A gentle bed is provided for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays a part on stage is a performer of that name.

clue.text: English novelist holy, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we want a word that is said the same as the synonym

parts.note: priestly means of a priest, holy

explanation.surface: An English novelist whose name suggests a saintly character.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley wrote 'The Good Companions' and 'An Inspector Calls'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Fat bird dropping in last of gravy

indicators.note: dropping means the next word is removed from the bird

parts.note: a puffin is a seabird

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of gravy

explanation.surface: A plump bird has fallen into the gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen and fleshy, as with puffy cheeks.

clue.text: Piece of advice to dump

definitions.meaning: a rubbish dump or a messy place

explanation.surface: Someone advises getting rid of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a helpful hint and, in Britain, a rubbish tip where waste is dumped.

clue.text: Approach Everest from here? Climbing it with risk

indicators.note: climbing means reading upwards in a down entry, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a bet is a risk taken

explanation.surface: Climbing Everest from a particular side involves risk.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern route up Everest starts from this region of China.

clue.text: Driver's aim, quite a distance?

parts.note: fair means considerable, quite large, as in a fair amount
a way is a distance, as in a long way

explanation.surface: A motorist is aiming for somewhere fairly far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist; it is a golfer's driver, the club used off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer hitting a driver from the tee hopes to land on the mown strip of grass leading to the green.

clue.text: One delivering a sermon as poor sportsman fails to finish

indicators.note: fails to finish means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a rabbit is slang for a poor player, especially a weak batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A preacher is compared to a hopeless athlete who never completes the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher leads services and gives sermons.

clue.text: Positive principle held by Himalayan guys

indicators.note: held by means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: An upbeat philosophy is kept by men living in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy it is the active, bright, masculine force, paired with yin.

clue.text: Putting in margarine initially, make a British meal

indicators.note: putting in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: create means make

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of margarine

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: add margarine first to make a traditional British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones with clotted cream and jam, served with a pot of tea, form an English afternoon meal, especially in Devon and Cornwall.
